scenario: AITA for not wanting to share an animal crossing town with my girlfriend? | This is kind of petty but here goes. The new animal crossing game is coming out and you can only have one village per nintendo switch console. my girlfriend and I both have a switch, but she wants to share one village with me so were both using one switch to play. I told her I would rather us both get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want to, but she disagreed. I even told her I would buy her the game but she said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in animal crossing which I just dont get. When I insisted we play on different consoles, even with valid reasoning and all that, she stormed out. called me an asshole baby, and told me to grow up. Animal crossing is a beloved series for me and I want to be able to make my village the way I want to, and I would also like to be able to play with my girlfriend online. AITA?

First, I need to remember the core dynamics here. Animal Crossing: New Horizons mechanics are key - one save file per Switch, so sharing means one village for both players. But the game actually has built-in multiplayer where you can visit each其他's islands online. 

Hmm... the girlfriend's "togeterness" request is interesting. She probably wants shared experiences in the same space - like building together physically, not just online. But James' perspective is valid too: he wants creative freedom to design his own town without compromise. 

*Pausing to check game mechanics*... right, you can't have two save files on one Switch for AC. So " sharing one village" literally means one person's save file. That's... not really " sharing" in the true sense. It's more like one person's game being co-opted. 

* mental note* - this is where the real issue lies. The girlfriend's phrasing "share one village" is technically accurate but emotionally misleading. It's not a shared space; it's her village or his village. 

Looking at the conflict points:
- James offered to buy her game (so she'd have her own Switch)
- She refused, wanting " togetherness" in one village
- When he insisted on separate consoles, she called him an asshole

*Ah-ha* - the real problem is the " togetherness" expectation. In AC, true togetherness is built through visiting each其他's islands, not forced coexistence in one save. The game was designed for this! 

*Checking community consensus*... yep, AC forums consistently say " never share saves" - it's a known pain point. Save files are personal. Forcing one save on two people is like demanding two people share a single diary. 

* Emotional angle*... her storming out over this feels disproportionate. It's a game, not a life-or-death issue. The " grow up" comment suggests she's framing a trivial disagreement as a character flaw. 

*Final judgment*... James is 100% not the asshole. His request is reasonable, his solution ( separate consoles) is the intended way to play, and her reaction is over the top. The " togetherness" she wants is actually better achieved through online play - which he's open to!

*Conclusion*... AITA? No. She's the one being unreasonable here. The " togetherness" she's seeking is a misunderstanding of how the game works. James' stance is technically correct and emotionally healthy.
